questions.question: 1. Which of the following best describes the main idea of the Naive String Searching Algorithm?

answers.a: It uses a prefix table to skip unnecessary comparisons.
answers.b: It checks for the pattern at every possible position in the text.
answers.c: It sorts the pattern and the text before searching.
answers.d: It uses hashing to find the pattern.

explanations.a: Incorrect. This describes the KMP algorithm, not the naive approach.
explanations.b: Correct. The naive algorithm checks for the pattern at every possible position in the text.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Sorting is not involved in naive string searching.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Hashing is used in algorithms like Rabin-Karp, not naive search.

questions.question: 2. What is the time complexity of the Naive String Searching Algorithm? (N = length of the string, M = length of the pattern)

explanations.a: Incorrect. O(N+M) is the complexity of more advanced algorithms like KMP.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(N^M) is not the correct complexity for this algorithm.
explanations.c: Correct. The naive string search checks each possible starting index in the string (O(N)), and for each, compares up to M characters (O(M)), resulting in O(N*M) time complexity.

questions.question: 4. Which of the following is a limitation of the Naive String Searching Algorithm compared to KMP?

answers.a: It cannot find patterns at all.
answers.b: It may perform redundant comparisons, leading to higher time complexity.
answers.c: It requires preprocessing of the pattern.
answers.d: It only works for numeric patterns.

explanations.a: Incorrect. The naive algorithm can find patterns, but less efficiently.
explanations.b: Correct. The naive algorithm may perform redundant comparisons, unlike KMP which avoids them.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Preprocessing is a feature of KMP, not a limitation of naive search.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The naive algorithm works for any pattern, not just numeric.

questions.question: 5. For which scenario is the naive string searching algorithm most likely to be as efficient as KMP?

answers.a: When the pattern is very long compared to the text.
answers.b: When the pattern and text have no repeated characters.
answers.c: When the pattern occurs many times in the text.
answers.d: When the text is much shorter than the pattern.

explanations.a: Incorrect. A long pattern compared to the text is not typical for efficiency.
explanations.b: Correct. If there are no repeated characters, the naive and KMP algorithms perform similarly.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Multiple occurrences do not make naive as efficient as KMP.
explanations.d: Incorrect. If the text is shorter than the pattern, no matches are possible.
